bib.title: Frequentist Inference (Computer Age Statistical Inference, ch. 2)

question: What does frequentist inference mean, how is it made practical when the true distribution F is unknown, and what optimality theory guides the choice of estimator or test?
contributions: Defines frequentist accuracy as the probabilistic accuracy of the estimator Theta-hat=t(X) attributed to the observed estimate
Lists five practical devices: plug-in, Taylor series (delta method), parametric/MLE theory, simulation/bootstrap, pivotal statistics
Sketches frequentist optimality: Fisher information bound for MLE and the Neyman-Pearson lemma

limits: Frequentist correctness does not tell you which algorithm t(x) to choose (mean vs Winsorized mean)
Pivotality, needed for exact frequentist correctness, is unavailable in most situations; the looser working definition is used
Optimality theory (MLE, Neyman-Pearson) has been strained by large data sets and complex questions; computer-age inference is described as ad hoc
Simplified picture only; list of devices is stated to be incomplete (asymptotics, approximate bootstrap CIs in Ch 11)
Criticism of the 'always reject at 95% means 5% errors' careerist definition: clients care about their own situation (footnote 6)
practices: Attribute to the single estimate the accuracy properties of the ensemble of Theta-hat=t(X) over hypothetical repeated datasets (p.14)
Estimate Var_F(X) unbiasedly by sum (xi-xbar)^2/(n-1) and plug into se(xbar)=[var/n]^(1/2) (p.15)
Use the delta method for smooth functions of means: se(s(theta-hat)) ~ |s'(theta)| sigma, plugging in estimates (p.15, p.20-21)
For non-smooth statistics (Winsorized mean, median) use the bootstrap: fit F-hat, simulate B=1000 replicates, take empirical SD (p.15-16)
Use pivotal statistics such as Student's t when normal-model assumptions hold, for exact tests and intervals (p.16-17)
Choose tests by the Neyman-Pearson likelihood-ratio rule, estimators by the MLE (p.18-19)

terms.definition: the accuracy of an observed estimate theta-hat=t(x) is the probabilistic accuracy of Theta-hat=t(X) as an estimator of theta
bias = mu - theta and var = E_F{(Theta-hat - mu)^2}, where mu = E_F{Theta-hat}
estimate the unknown F-dependent accuracy formula from the observed data, e.g. var-hat in se formula
first-order Taylor series approximation var{s(theta-hat)} ~ |s'(mu)|^2 sigma^2
find an estimate F-hat of F, simulate Theta-hat(k)=t(X(k)) from F-hat for k=1..B, take empirical SD as standard error
a statistic whose distribution does not depend upon the underlying distribution F
only rules t_c(x) thresholding log likelihood ratio L(x)=f1/f0 at c can be optimum; any other rule has some t_c with smaller errors of both kinds
observations below the 25th percentile moved up to it, those above the 75th moved down, then the mean taken
